<!--
  Heads up: habenula-oss is a read-only release mirror. Development happens
  in the upstream monorepo, and each release lands here as a single snapshot
  commit — so maintainers never merge external pull requests on this
  repository.

  Your pull request is still the right way to propose a code change. It is
  a proposal, not a merge:
    1. Open the pull request. The CLA bot adds a one-time signing step
       (signing confirms the project may use your contribution; it does not
       mean the change is accepted).
    2. A maintainer reviews it. If accepted, the change is applied upstream
       and ships in a later release, and this pull request is closed with a
       note saying so.

  You are credited for an accepted change. Your code is not merged here, but
  at the release that carries it, a commit authored by you is added to `main`
  here. That commit adds one line to CONTRIBUTORS.md naming you, what you
  contributed, and your proposal. It contains nothing else. Because you are
  its author, it counts toward your GitHub contributions. Your change is also
  credited by name in the release notes of the package it ships in.

  Your handle and the author email on your commits both become part of this
  repository's permanent public history. GitHub attributes a commit by its
  author email. If that email is not linked to your GitHub account, the
  commit does not appear on your profile. Check it before you propose a
  change.

  For bugs, feature ideas, or questions, open an issue instead. For security
  vulnerabilities, do NOT open a PR or issue — email security@habenula.ai.

  See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full flow.
-->
